headline: Adding AGT-f76fe737-1 to 1 existing rule(s) changed held-out rule-set recall by +10.8 pp and false-positive rate by +0.83 pp (+70 alerts). Awaiting human review.

advisory.title: Criminals Increasing SIM Swap Schemes to Steal Millions of Dollars from US Public
advisory.publisher: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3), Alert I-020822-PSA
advisory.excerpt:
The Federal Bureau of Investigation is issuing this announcement to inform mobile carriers and the public of the increasing use of Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) swapping by criminals to steal money from fiat and virtual currency accounts. From January 2018 to December 2020, the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) received 320 complaints related to SIM swapping incidents with adjusted losses of approximately $12 million. In 2021, IC3 received 1,611 SIM swapping complaints with adjusted losses of more than $68 million.
SIM swapping is a malicious technique where criminal actors target mobile carriers to gain access to victims' bank accounts, virtual currency accounts, and other sensitive information. Criminal actors primarily conduct SIM swap schemes using social engineering, insider threat, or phishing techniques.
Once the SIM is swapped, the victim's calls, texts, and other data are diverted to the criminal's device. This access allows criminals to send 'Forgot Password' or 'Account Recovery' requests to the victim's email and other online accounts associated with the victim's mobile telephone number. Using SMS-based two-factor authentication, mobile application providers send a link or one-time passcode via text to the victim's number, now owned by the criminal, to access accounts. The criminal uses the codes to login and reset passwords, gaining control of online accounts associated with the victim's phone profile.

dataset.description: Synthetic payments scenario (~3.4% fraud) with velocity, decline, card-present, time-of-day, device, SIM-change, credential-reset, and new-payee features. Three fraud modes: high-value misuse, injected card testing, and injected SIM-swap account takeover.
dataset.limitations: Fully synthetic. The card-testing and SIM-swap account-takeover patterns were injected to demonstrate how the workflow surfaces coverage gaps, and legitimate look-alikes were added for each; results do not measure real-world detection.

findings.technique_name: Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) Swapping and Account Takeover
findings.summary: The FBI IC3 alert describes how criminals use SIM swapping via social engineering or phishing to divert a victim's mobile number, intercept SMS 2FA codes, reset credentials, and take over financial accounts.
behaviors: Criminals target mobile carriers using social engineering, insider threat, or phishing techniques to perform SIM swaps.
Victim calls, texts, and data are diverted to the criminal's device.
Criminals send password reset or account recovery requests and use SMS-based two-factor authentication to take over accounts.
indicators: Recent mobile SIM change or port associated with the account phone number.
Credential resets or account recovery requests in preceding 24 hours.
Transactions originating from a new device following SIM swap.
testable_hypotheses: Transactions occurring shortly after a SIM change exhibit a significantly higher fraud rate.
Combining a recent SIM change with credential resets or new device access identifies account takeover fraud.
uncertainties: Public advisory statistics represent national victim complaints and do not map directly to individual transaction-level features.
Exact mobile carrier indicators and social engineering tactics are not fully captured in tabular transaction logs.

agent_conclusion.rationale: The intelligence document describes SIM swapping schemes used to compromise accounts and conduct unauthorized transfers. We identified that the dataset includes `days_since_sim_change` and `credential_resets_24h` fields, which allow direct testing of SIM swap indicators. Candidate rule AGT-f76fe737-1 (`days_since_sim_change <= 1`) successfully improves validation recall from 32.51% to 45.81% while maintaining an acceptable false positive rate.
limitations: Synthetic dataset metrics may not reflect live production distributions.
Public advisory reports aggregate historical trends and do not provide individual transaction ground truth.

baseline_rule.name: High transaction amount baseline
baseline_rule.description: Flags a transaction when its amount is at least 1,500 synthetic currency units.
baseline_rule.rationale: A simple, documented starting point for comparing candidate rules. The threshold is illustrative and is not calibrated for real financial data.
